newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong preparing to hold March elections - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong preparing to hold March elections - paper.

text.p: Hong Kong could hold its first elections under Chinese rule in March and install a new parliament by next May or June, a newspaper said on Friday.
The Chinese-language daily Ming Pao quoted a senior official, Solicitor General Daniel Fung, as saying authorities had already begun drafting an election law for polls in March.
Hong Kong's elected legislature was scrapped on July 1 halfway through a four-year term when the territory reverted to China after 156 years as a British colony.
To the dismay of pro-democracy campaigners here and Western states, Parliament was replaced by an interim council chosen by a Beijing-controlled committee, pending polls next year.
Beijing said democratic reforms used for the last polls in 1995 violated Sino-British accords on the sovereignty change and promised a fresh ballot within a year of the handover.
China's action was strongly denounced in numerous foreign capitals as well as by local democracy activists.
Western leaders who attended Hong Kong's handover ceremony this week called for new elections as soon as possible.
Hong Kong Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa told Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer that elections would be held next May.
Ming Pao said the administration planned to have new election laws passed by the Provisional Legislature in October with polls held half a year later.
Ming Pao did not give details of the draft law, but there are wide expectations the new rules will be framed to favour Beijing's supporters in Hong Kong and hamper the pro-democracy parties.

Martin Lee, leader of the popular Democratic Party, ousted as a legislator because of China's appointment of the interim body, predicted on Thursday his group could win only 12 seats in the 60-seat legislature in the next elections under the likely new rules, compared with 19 held by his party before.
